why_this_label: 9.3 mmol/L is what 168 mg/dL converts to. It is arithmetically right and it is not what the page says, and rule (a) of the committed prompt names exactly this: a unit conversion the source did not perform. The conversion is the project's documented VLM failure mode (MedRepBench's character-level unit misreads, mg/dL vs mmol/L), and a value the page does not carry cannot be cited to it.
what_this_detects: A judge that has stopped working, on a failure mode this project is specifically exposed to. It is NOT a drift detector. Measured over five independent best-of-3 gradings each way: the committed prompt grades it fail 5/5 rounds and 15/15 votes, but a generic one-line rubric splits — fail on two rounds of five, 7/15 votes — so a loosened prompt does not reliably move it. The fixture stays because it is stable and because mg/dL vs mmol/L is the documented VLM misread this suite exists to catch; it is classed with fc_pass and fc_fail rather than with the two fixtures that discriminate.
